`Result.K8sUnrendered` and logged, which is what keeps "nothing found
  there" apart from "nobody looked there".
- **A chart or overlay that does not render is a finding, not a failed
  scan** (`K8S-RENDER`, HIGH, on `Chart.yaml` or the kustomization). Measured
  on helm 4.3.0: a missing dependency is only a WARNING for `helm lint`, and
  it is `helm template` that fails — so the render failure is reported unless
  lint already raised an ERROR. `helm lint` also names that chart by its
  **absolute** path (`/scan/charts/x` in a container), which `helmLintPath`
  brings back to the repository. The finding's Resolution is in the
  renderer's terms (`renderResolution`): helm's speaks of dependencies,
  kustomize's of `kustomize build`; a file kustomize's load restrictor refuses
  (`security; file … is not in or below …`, as `kubectl apply -k` would) gets a
  directory with its own kustomization or, when the deployment tool does the
  same, `scan.tools.kustomize.args: [--load-restrictor=LoadRestrictionsNone]`.
  The finding stays HIGH (DEVDESK-742).
- **A renderer in a container sees the target's git repository**
  (`renderScope`, DEVDESK-742): `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, run in the
  target through the runner, names the root mounted read-only at `/scan`, and
  `-w /scan/<target relative to it>` keeps every argument and finding path
  relative to the target, so an overlay's `../../base` or a chart's
  `file://../lib` outside the target builds as with a binary.
  - **Guards.** `widerScope` keeps the target alone when git fails or is
    absent, when the root is `/`, the home directory or above it (or the home
    is unknown), or when the root, symlinks resolved, is not a strict
    ancestor of the target. It also keeps the target alone when git was
    redirected, which a cloned repository can do: `git config --get
    core.worktree` set or unreadable, or a root that does not hold the `.git`
    itself (`gitDirIsHere`: a directory, or a worktree's `.git` file whose git
    directory names it back; a symlink is refused). Those git calls run
    without `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR` and `GIT_CONFIG*`;
    `GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES` is kept, since it can only narrow.
  - **An overlay that still fails is HIGH**, with kustomize's whole message:
    DevDesk does not walk the repository to tell a reference its mount hid
    from a broken one. When a kustomize image reports `evalsymlink failure`
    or `no such file or directory`, the Resolution adds that the reference
    may point outside what DevDesk mounts, and suggests scanning the
    enclosing directory or `scan.tools.kustomize.source: binary`
    (`mountResolution`); a binary never gets that sentence.
  - **Known limits.** The renderer container keeps the network (no
    `--network none`). helm follows symlinks inside the mount, so a hostile
    chart can bring a sibling file's content into its error, as a binary,
    which sees the whole host, already could. The enclosing git repository is
    mounted as it is: the target's neighbours under the git root become
### The finding detail (DEVDESK-750, DEVDESK-751)

`Enter` on a finding opens a scrollable detail (`internal/ui/security/details.go`).
It used to overflow the viewport (the text width had a floor of 40 cells, `Match`,
`Run:`, `Package` and `Version` had no width at all, and the viewport itself was
given the view's width instead of two cells less), print a render failure's whole
stderr as a title, and bury the one thing a reader wants, what to do, under the
facts.

**Layout, measured.** The router hands the details state `H - 12` rows
(`shortcut.HeaderRows` 7, one blank row, a two-row footer, the title line and the
bottom border) and the viewport frame takes two columns, so the viewport is `W - 2`
wide (`sizeDetails`, called from `enter` and from `WindowSizeMsg`, so a resize
while the detail is open is right too); `Padding(1)` takes one cell and one row
on each side:

| Terminal | Viewport rows | Text rows visible (after the top padding) | Text width |
|---|---|---|---|
| 80x24 | 12 | 11 | 76 |
| 120x40 | 28 | 27 | 116 |
| 175x50 | 38 | 37 | 171 |

**Order (DEVDESK-751).** What to do comes before why. The header (severity, ID), the
title on one line, a blank line, then the Fix block, `Why`, `Output` and `Refs`. A
section is emitted only when it has content, and sections are joined by exactly one
blank line (never two); the sub-fields of the Fix block follow its first line with no
blank line. The text width is `detailsTextWidth()` = `min(max(W-4, 1), maxColumnWidth)`,
`maxColumnWidth` being 110: 76, 110 and 110 cells at 80, 120 and 175 columns. Every value
is wrapped at that width, hanging under its label (`detailsText`, `details_text.go`); a
tab and a run of blank lines are normalised first. At 80x24 `Fix:` is on the fourth text
line and `Where:` on the fifth, both inside the 11 visible lines.

```
HIGH KSV-0001
Container 'api' of Deployment 'web' should…
                                                <- blank
Fix: Built-in fix unavailable: <reason>         <- the status, in the closed vocabulary below
Where: k8s/deploy.yaml:12                       <- File[:Line], then Package, Job, Script, Match
Do: 1. <MissingFor | "Update x to 1.2">         <- numbered steps, then the Resolution, word for word
    <Resolution, wrapped, hanging>
Run: $ go get golang.org/x/net@v0.23.0          <- one line, cut with an ellipsis; omitted with no command
Effect: <rule.Title | Fixed in X>
Warning: <rule.Warning>
                                                <- blank
Why:                                            <- Description, Pod Security, Source, Type
Output:                                         <- Message, 8 lines at most, then "… N more lines"
Refs:
```

The builders are `detailsFix` (status, `detailsWhere`, `Do` from `fixSteps` and the
Resolution, `detailsRun`, Effect, Warning), `detailsWhy`, `detailsOutput` and
`detailsReferences`, each under 50 lines. The Fix block is written in `ColorText` alone
and its labels in `theme.DetailLabelStyle` (bold, `ColorText`): `ColorDim`, `ColorSubTitleFg`,
`ColorTitleFg` and `ColorWarn` fall under 4.5:1 on several shipped themes, so the word
`Warning:` carries the warning, not a colour. The measure is frozen in
`docs/measurements/2026-11-23-sec-detail-contrast.md`; retuning the palette is a separate story.
`DetailLabelStyle` is declared twice in `theme/styles.go` (the var and the rebuild in
`ApplyTheme`), like every style, or it keeps the default theme's colours.

**Display only.** `shortPaths(text, target)` removes `<target>/` and the container
mount `/scan/` from the title, the Message and the File, folds a path under HOME to
`~/`, and ignores a target that is not an absolute path (an image reference). The
finding keeps its text, the scan cache is untouched, and
`scan.renderFailure` still writes the absolute paths, which is what the cache holds. The title is `oneLine`: the first line, cut with `theme.Ellipsis`. The Message is
`cappedLines`: wrapped at `min(width, 110)` cells, 8 lines at most, then `… N more
lines` (wrapped lines, not source lines). A Message equal to the title or to the
description is not repeated. Widths are measured with `x/ansi`, as the viewport
does, never with the `runewidth`-based `theme` helpers.

**The fix status.** `fixStatusOf(f, onDisk)` (`details_fix.go`) says it in words, in a closed
vocabulary, never in a colour or a key name (Rules 130, 134). Every label is one of the five
constants, or `Built-in fix unavailable: ` followed by a non-empty reason
(`TestEveryFixLabelIsInTheClosedVocabulary`):

| Finding | Label | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| misconfiguration, the target is an image (catalog rule or not) | `Cannot fix here` | `reasonFileNotOnDisk`, in the footer on `ctrl+o` |
| misconfiguration, catalog rule, the rule declines this instance | `Built-in fix unavailable: <reason>` | the `Declines` reason |
| misconfiguration, catalog rule, directory, no refusal | `Built-in fix available` | Effect = `rule.Title`, Warning = `rule.Warning` |
| misconfiguration, no catalog rule, some guidance (`MissingFor`, Resolution or FixCommand) | `Manual` | Do = the missing text, then the Resolution |
| misconfiguration, no catalog rule, no guidance | `No guidance available` | |
| vulnerability with `FixedIn` | `Manual` | Effect = `Fixed in <version>` |
| vulnerability without | `No fix published` | |
| secret, license, CI | `Manual` with guidance, else `No guidance available` | |

A misconfiguration's status reads `misconfigFixAvailability` (extracted from `canFixMisconfig`),
so the status line, the `ctrl+o` shortcut and the footer refusal are one computation. The
invariants are tested: `Built-in fix available` holds exactly when `ctrl+o` is enabled in the
detail, and for `Built-in fix unavailable: R` and `Cannot fix here` the footer after `ctrl+o` is
exactly `R` and `reasonFileNotOnDisk` (`TestFixStatusAndTheShortcutAgree`,
`TestTheFooterAfterCtrlOSaysTheReasonOfTheFixLine`). A vulnerability with a `FixedIn` is
`Manual` because the vocabulary has no "fix available"; DEVDESK-750's `Fix available`,
`No fix available`, `No built-in fix`, `No built-in fix here` and `No built-in fix for this instance`
are gone.

**Command or sentence.** `scan.IsFixInstruction(f)` says whether `FixCommand` is the
`Update <pkg> to <version>` sentence written for an ecosystem with no known command
(`fixInstruction`, same bytes as before: the cache is unchanged). `fixAction` shows a
command as `Run: <cmd>` and a sentence as a step under `Do`. `runCommand(f)` is the one
computation behind the `Run` line and `Y`: the trimmed `FixCommand` when `fixAction` says `Run`
and it is plain words (`plainWords`), `("", false)` otherwise. It refuses a line break, any control
character (`unicode.IsControl`: an escape sequence, a tab, a carriage return, a NUL), any character
with no visible form or a blank other than a single space (`!unicode.IsPrint`: no-break space,
zero-width and right-to-left marks, line separator) and any shell metacharacter
(`shellMeta`: `; | & $ ` < > ( ) \ ' " { } * ? ! #`). The list is a second defense for a command that
did not come through `scan.FixCommand`, such as one read from a cache written by another build;
`TestRunCommandRefusesWhatAShellOrATerminalReadsAsMoreThanWords` holds its cases. A refused command
is not lost: `fixSteps` puts its text under `Do` like a sentence (control characters removed, see
below), `Y` is greyed with `reasonNoCommand`, and there is no `Run` line. The screen cuts the `Run`
line to the width of the column while `Y` copies all of it, which is why a tail could hide there
before this check.

**Scanner text on screen.** `normalizeText` and `oneLine` (`details_text.go`) go through
`withoutControlSpace`: an escape sequence (CSI, OSC) is removed whole with `ansi.Strip`, a tab
becomes four spaces, and every other control character (C0, C1, `\r`), line and paragraph separator
and format character (bidi and zero-width marks; the two joiners stay for emoji) is dropped. The line
feed stays for `normalizeText`. Nothing a scanner wrote can set the window title or reorder the text
(`TestNoScannerFieldReachesTheScreenWithAnEscapeSequence`).

**Actions from the detail (DEVDESK-751).** Six keys, the same for every finding, in this order:
`esc Back`, `W Open ref`, `enter Open file`, `ctrl+o Apply fix`, `Y Copy cmd`, `X Exclude`
(`detailsShortcuts`, `header.go`). The descriptions are at most ten cells: at 80 columns the
shortcut column is `78 - 19 (info) - 40 (logo) = 19` cells wide, `<ctrl+o>` takes nine of them, and
seven rows leave room for six entries beside `ctrl+p Commands` (`TestTheDetailHeaderHoldsItsSixKeysAtEveryWidth`
in `internal/app`). There is no `O`: `enter` opens the viewer, which has it. Each key is greyed,
never removed (Rule 130), by one `shortcut.Availability` that the header and the handler both read,
and a refused key puts its reason in the footer at level Warn and opens nothing. None of the
availabilities reads the disk, so a header redraw does no I/O.

| Key | Availability | Reasons | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enter` | `canOpenFindingFile` (`findingFilePath`) | `reasonNoFile`, `reasonFileOutsideTarget`, `reasonFileNotOnDisk` | in the Cmd, `staysInside` follows the links, then `uiviewer.OpenRequestMsg{Source: viewer.NewFileSource(path)}`; the viewer reports a missing file. A link that leaves the target gives `FindingFileRefusedMsg` and a Warn with `reasonFileLinkOutsideTarget` |
| `ctrl+o` | `canFixMisconfig` | `reasonNotMisconfigTab`, `reasonFileNotOnDisk`, the `Declines` reason, `noFixReason` | `prepareMisconfigFix`: the Misconfigurations tab's preview, confirmation (default No), write and re-scan |
| `Y` | `canCopyFixCommand` (`runCommand`) | `reasonNoCommand` | `writeClipboard(command)` in the Cmd, then `FixCommandCopiedMsg` |
| `X` | `canExclude` | `reasonNotASecret`, `reasonNotGitleaks` | `handleIgnoreSecret`: the confirmation of the results state, byte for byte |

`subjectFinding()` is what these actions act on: the finding on screen in the details state
(`selectedFinding`), the selected row in the results state. The detail never goes back through
`findingsTable.Selected()`, because a re-scan puts the table back at the top
(`setResult` runs `updateFindingsTable`, which runs `GotoTop`). In the detail the active tab is
the one the finding was opened from, so the tab checks of `canFixMisconfig` and `canExclude` stay
true to it. `ctrl+o` is a declared exception on the surface `security/details` (`app-shell.md`).
`reasonNotMisconfigTab` reads `Only misconfigurations have a built-in fix`, a wording that holds in
the detail as well as on a tab.

**Links.** `findingFilePath` is lexical (no I/O, so the header can call it on every frame): a
parent segment or an absolute path elsewhere is refused there. A link inside the target that points
outside it is only found by looking at the disk, so the Cmd of `enter` does it: `staysInside` applies
`filepath.EvalSymlinks` to the path and to the target and tests the relation again. A part of the
## Scan Cache

Two independent disk+memory caches in `internal/cache/`:
- `ImageScanCache` — keyed by `"repo:tag"`, metadata at `~/.devdesk/cache/image-scans.json`, full results in `image-results/<sha256>.json`
- `WorkspaceScanCache` — keyed by absolute repo path, metadata at `~/.devdesk/cache/workspace-scans.json`, full results in `workspace-results/<sha256>.json`

Both entries carry the four severity counts and `Sensitive *bool`, the secret
verdict written by `scan.Result.SecretVerdict()` (see Security Scanning). `nil`
is a value: it means no stage looked, and it is what every image entry written
before there was an image secret stage decodes to.

**One is scoped to a configuration context and the other is not, and the
asymmetry is the point** (§3.39). What decides it is whether the *key* is
per context:

| Cache | Key | Scoped |
|---|---|---|
| `WorkspaceScanCache` | absolute repo path, reached through `workspaces_dir` | **yes** — `workspaces_dir` is per context, so the same path may be different work |
| `ImageScanCache` | a local Docker reference | **no** — `docker image ls` answers for the machine, not for a configuration |

Scoping the image cache was the mistake. Two contexts looking at `nginx:1.25`
are looking at the same bytes, so a context switch dropped counts for images
that had not moved — and the full results beside the index were **never** scoped
at all: they are content-addressed by image name, with no context anywhere. The
index and the blobs disagreed, and the index was the one that was wrong.

So `NewImageScanCache()` takes no context — a parameter that has to be ignored
is worse than none — while `NewWorkspaceScanCache(contextName)` keeps its own.

**Which name, and when it is read** (D68). A scan's writer takes the context it
was *launched* in, handed down from `jobs.Run.Context`; it does not read the
current one. A batch of twelve repositories runs for minutes and a context
switch during it is ordinary — that is what a background scan is for — so a
writer reading `config.CurrentContextName()` when Trivy returned put the counts
under whichever context happened to be on screen. Both halves of that are
silent: the launching context loses results it asked for and rescans forever,
and the arriving one gains results for paths that may mean nothing there.

Three writers shared it — `scanOneRepoCmd`, `storeRescan`, and
`deleteScanCacheCmd`, the purge half of `ctrl+a`. The purge was the worst of the
three: it travelled in the same `tea.Batch` as the scan replacing it, each
reading the name on its own goroutine, with nothing making them agree. They now
travel in one builder (`purgeAndScan` in `ws`), so there is one name between
them rather than two that happen to match.

Reading the current context is still right for a **load** —
`loadScanCacheCmd`, `loadInventoryCmd` — and for anything that *names* the
context. The line is not "inside a `Cmd`"; it is whether the code writes a
result someone asked for under a name.

`internal/cache/scan_file.go` owns the scoped shape
(`{version, contexts: {name: {key: entry}}}`): the workspace cache writes it, and
the image cache still *reads* it in order to fold it back.
`image_scan.go` owns the flat one (`{version: 2, entries: {key: entry}}`) and
understands all three shapes it has had — v2 as it stands, v1 folded into one
map, and the bare `{key: entry}` map that predates contexts, which is already
this shape and needs only a version stamped on it.

**A collision in the fold is settled, not reported**: two contexts holding the
same image is the ordinary case — it is one image, and both saw it — so the more
recent `ScannedAt` wins. The image did not change between them; the vulnerability
database did.

The fold is **written back on the first open** rather than deferred to the next
`Set`, for the reason the context migration was: a file left in the old shape is
folded again on every open, so what it holds would depend on when it was last
read.

**A shared entry may have been produced under another context's scan options.**
`categories`, `tools.trivy.ignore_unfixed` and the rest are per context, so counts written
elsewhere can differ from what this context would produce. That is the accepted
cost: the `Scanned` column carries the age, and `S` rescans. The secret verdict
is unaffected — `Sensitive` is `nil` when no stage looked, which is what a scan
run with secrets off writes anyway.

Cache invalidation: `S` (single) overwrites; `A` (all) rescans, and purges the cache first when its checkbox is ticked.



## Who knows a scan is running — `internal/jobs`
everything the fix needs and stay the thing that measures.

| Field | What it answers |
|---|---|
| `line`, `end_line` | the **span** of the faulted block. `line` alone says where the problem starts, which is enough to read it and not enough to replace it |
| `message` | this instance's own wording ("Specify at least 1 USER command"), where `description` is the rule's generic text |
| `status` | what the scanner concluded for the rule on this target |
| `id` | the AVD id — the rule's stable identity, and what a re-scan is checked against |
| `resolution`, `references` | the prose fix and the advisory |
| `pss_profile` | `baseline` or `restricted`: the Pod Security Standards profile that requires the rule behind a Kubernetes finding (DEVDESK-686). Absent (`omitempty`) when the finding is not a Pod Security one |

**`pss_profile` is the profile DevDesk shows, not Trivy's raw anchor.** It comes
from `remediation.PodSecurity`, the same call as the security view's label and
filter, so a KSV-0104 finding whose seccomp profile is missing reads `restricted`
although Trivy anchors the rule `#baseline`. The setting `scan.pss_profile` does
not change it: the field is the same under `all`. A finding with an unknown
KSV-0104 origin, and KSV-0117 and KSV-0119 (no anchor), are covered in
`scanning.md`.

- `internal/scan/kubeconform.go`: `validateFiles` calls the new `stampSchemaRepro`, which stamps `K8S-SCHEMA` findings only.
- `internal/scan/gitleaks.go`, `internal/scan/trivy.go`: secrets get `Steps: secretSteps()`.
- `internal/ui/security/details_repro.go`: `reproCommand`, `copyCommand` and `detailsRepro` written.
- Shared detail files, minimal edits:
  - `details_fix.go`: `fixSteps` prepends `f.Steps` as a copy, and `hasGuidance` counts `Steps`.
  - `details.go`: one line in `detailsFix` calls `detailsRepro`.
  - `details_actions.go`: `canCopyFixCommand` and `copyFixCommand` read `copyCommand`.
  - `header.go`: the "Finding details" help text now mentions Steps, Repro and `Y`.
- `internal/mcp/scan_tools.go`: only `Steps []string json:"steps,omitempty"`, filled with `slices.Clone`.
- Docs: `docs/architecture/scanning.md` and `docs/architecture/mcp.md`.
  - `scanning.md` covers the Steps/Repro/RanFrom fields, "Repro only if the local tool ran", the detail section, the Scan Cache paragraph (no version, backward compatible), and a "Writing a Resolution, Steps and Repro" section marked "proposed, to be confirmed".
  - `mcp.md` documents `steps` only.

**Deviations**
- **MCP test changed, as you decided (b):** I edited `internal/mcp/scan_steps_test.go`. It now requires `steps` present, and `repro`, `ran_from` and the command text absent from the answer and the schema. The test was renamed `TestScanResultCarriesTheStepsOfAFindingDevDeskWroteAndNotItsRepro`. The schema test is now `...ExplainsStepsAndNothingMore`. It checks "remediation steps" in place of "root/never runs/container". The header comment says why.
- **Tests I did not change:** no other test was modified beyond those already in the worktree.
- **`reproCommand` trims only spaces**, not all whitespace, because the test "a carriage" requires `"…dev\r"` to be refused.
- **`reproCommand` returns false when `RanFrom == container`**, even if the cache holds a `Repro`. `copyCommand` then gives `reasonToolInContainer`.
- **Decision (d):** a `Repro` read back from a cache is revalidated by `PlainWords` at display time (details above).

**Open points**
- A `RanFrom == container` result with a stale `Repro` shows `Repro: none: …` and greys `Y` with `reasonToolInContainer`. I read this as the intended behavior.
- `details.go`, `details_fix.go`, `details_actions.go` and `header.go` are also touched by DEVDESK-753, so expect small conflicts on `detailsFix`, `fixSteps` and the help text.
- `RanFrom` is recorded on every `K8S-RENDER` and `HELM-LINT` finding and on every plain-file `K8S-SCHEMA` finding, with or without a `Repro`. This is how the detail tells a container run from a path that cannot be written plainly.
